note:
A kilim from the town of Pirot is recognized by its geometric patterns. The main motif is the eight-pointed star, a symbol of protection and fertility.

Other patterns:
• коларић
• бу̑рма
• бѝбер
• ло̀за

The oldest surviving kilim dates from 1650. These kilims were luxury items.
title: The Pirot kilim

related.en: male name, insulting as a form of address

note:
A Serb will not take offense at ја̏рац: it is a neutral word for a billy goat.

Insults for a man are instead:
• ма̀јмун
• ма̀гарац
• ко̏њ

Vocative: ма̀јмуне, магарче, коњу. Ма̀јмун is masculine, so you would not say it to a woman.

Also, Шабан is a name, but calling an adult «Шабане!» is a rude insult.
title: Which animals are insults in Serbia

related.en: the snowman as a character, Frosty

note:
Many of the names are playful Serbian versions of the originals:
• Пепѐљуга
• Снежана
• Палчица
• Златокоса
• Душко Дугоушко
• Паја Патак
• Пера Детлић
• Сунђер Боб Коцкалоне - from ко̏цка (cube) and пантало́не (pants)
• Сне̏шко Бѐлић - «Бѐлић» looks like a surname

The English equivalents are in the related words.
title: Fairy-tale and cartoon characters in Serbian

related.en: Baba Roga, the Serbian Baba Yaga

note:
Serbs call Baba Yaga баба Рога.

A popular children's poem by Ljubivoje Ršumović is about a brave boy. The old woman lives in a пећина (cave) and hides in the dark. The boy brings her a lemon and a pear, and she will not even show her њушка: she is afraid of him.

The poem rhymes and is easy to learn by heart.
title: Baba Roga, the Serbian Baba Yaga

note:
Serbs are keen on horoscopes and usually know not only their sign but also their rising sign (the ascendant).

The signs:
• Водолија, Рибе, О́ван, Би̏к
• Близа̀нци, Ра̏к, Ла̏в, Дѐвица
• Ва́га, Шкорпија, Стре́лац, Ја̏рац

A joke: «ду̏плӣ Ја̏рац» means a Capricorn by both sign and rising sign. It is almost a diagnosis, and nothing good is associated with it.
title: Zodiac signs and the «double Capricorn»

note:
Short forms are not always predictable:
• Марија shortens to Мара and Маја, while Ма́ша is a separate name
• Јелена, Елена and Лена are different names
• Са̏ша is a male name, Ва̏ња is a full female name

Suffixes:
• -ка (Сашка, Машка) sounds warm
• -ица makes a diminutive (Машица)

Girls' names can also be fruits and berries: Ја̏года, Ви̏шња, Ма̀лина, Ду̏ња.

Documents ask for и̏ме, прѐзиме and и̏ме о̀ца (father's name).
title: Serbian names: what to know

note:
A cat is called with «мац-мац» and a dog with «кс-кс»: the familiar «here, kitty» means nothing to a Serbian cat. For a cat there is also the diminutive ма́ца.

Sounds:
• па̏с ла̏је̄: ав-ав (woof)
• ма́ца мјауче и преде (meows and purrs)
• со́ва: ху-ху (hoot)
• кра̏ва: му (moo)
• гу̏ска: га-га (honk)
• пе́тао: кукурику (cock-a-doodle-doo)
• ко̀ко̄шка: ко̏-ко̏-ко̏ (cluck)
• пра̑се: грок-грок (oink)
• ко̏њ: њи-њи (neigh)
• ми̏ш: цију (squeak)
• пи̏ле: пи̏јӯ (peep)
• па̏тка: ква-ква (quack)
• жа̏ба: кре-кре (ribbit)
title: What animals say in Serbian

related.en: «The Seven Deadly Sins», a snack bar in Novi Sad

note:
In central Novi Sad there is a snack bar called «Седам смртних грехова»: every sandwich is named after a sin.
• го́рдо̄ст (pride), за́вист (envy), прождрљивост (gluttony)
• по̏жуда (lust), гне̑в (wrath), по̏хлепа (greed), ле̏њо̄ст (sloth)

On the door there is a pun: instead of дије́та it says дијете (child, in the ijekavian form). The result reads as «not the right place for a diet or for a child».
title: The Seven Deadly Sins

related.en: the time before noon, including the morning

note:
Approximate boundaries:
• ју̏тро - until 10 a.m.
• препо́дне - until noon (including the morning)
• по́дне - 12:00
• попо́дне - from 12 to 17
• ве̏че̄ - around 18-19
• по̏но̄ћ - 00:00

«Препо́дне» as one word is a part of the day, while «пре̏ по́дне» is a time phrase: before noon.

For seasons that have just passed, Serbs say ле̏то̄с, зѝмӯс, јесѐнас, про̀лето̄с: this summer, this winter and so on, once the season is over.

«На вре́ме» means on time.
title: Times of day in Serbian

skip: Serbian words that sound funny to Russian ears and false friends with Russian; makes sense only for a Russian speaker

note:
Fingers (прсти):
• па̏лац
• ка̀жипрст - literally «pointing finger»
• сре̏дњӣ пр̏ст
• домали прст
• ма̑лӣ пр̏ст

The rest: пѐсница (fist), дла̏н (palm), ша̏ка (hand).

The wedding ring (бу̑рма) is worn on the домали прст; in Serbia Orthodox Christians wear it on the right hand.
title: Fingers and the hand

note:
In small towns a death is announced with a death notice (смр̀товница) on poles and notice boards.

A notice shows:
• a photo of the deceased
• the years of life
• the date and place of the funeral (са̀храна)
• the names of the grieving relatives

Newspapers have a similar section with photos.

The usual words of condolence: «Примите моје саучешће».
title: Death notices in Serbia

related.en: to cheer for, to root for

note:
Nicknames of the fans of the Belgrade clubs:
• гробари (gravediggers) - Partizan
• цигани - Red Star

The word хулигани is harsh: it is used for fans who riot. It is not used for a child.

Навѝјати means to cheer for a team: «За кога навијаш?»
title: Football fans and their nicknames

note:
On February 14 Serbia celebrates Дан заљубљених. In the church calendar this is the day of Све̑тӣ Три̏фӯн, the patron saint of vine growers and winemakers.

People wish each other «Срећан Дан заљубљених».
title: Saint Trifun and Valentine's Day

note:
In Serbia taxis are ordered by phone.

What to tell the dispatcher:
• the street
• the building number
• the entrance (у̀лаз)

The apartment number and the destination are not needed. The car arrives within a few minutes, so call only when you are ready to leave.

In the car:
1. Say hello and give the address.
2. Check the fare on the meter: day, night or holiday.
3. Leave a tip by rounding up the amount.
title: How to order a taxi

note:
Einstein was married to a Serbian woman, Mileva Marić, whom he met as a student in 1896.

So people joke:
• a foreigner married to a Serbian woman is a «ср̏пскӣ зе̏т»
• a foreign woman married to a Serb is a «српска снајка»

Many schools in Serbia are named after famous people instead of being numbered, Mileva Marić-Einstein among them.
title: Einstein, the Serbian son-in-law

note:
In Serbia March 8 is a working day, but it is customary to give flowers, and restaurants hand them out to women.

Young people today often congratulate only their mother and their teacher.

On the eve, March 7, men are jokingly «congratulated» on the holiday that is about to begin.
title: March 8 in Serbia

related.en: a couple of basins and three buckets

note:
A joke for Serbian friends: say «пар лавора и три канте» fast, and it sounds like an Italian phrase.

Said slowly in Serbian it means «a couple of basins and three buckets». The words ла̏вор and ка́нта (bucket; ка́нта за смѐће is a trash can) came from Italian.
title: Italian-sounding humor: «пар лавора и три канте»

related.en: pre-election silence (the day of quiet before the vote)

note:
Basic election vocabulary:
• стра̏нка, па̀ртија - party
• бѝра̄ч, гла̀са̄ч - voter
• бирачко место - polling station
• изборна комисија - election commission
• гласачки листић - ballot
• гла̀сати, гла̀са̄ње - to vote, voting
• гласачко тело - electorate
• резултати гласања - voting results
• предизборна тишина - the quiet period before the vote

«Поно̀вити гла̀са̄ње» means to vote again.
title: Elections: a mini-glossary

related.en: the red egg kept as a protective charm

note:
At Easter (У̏скрс, church name Ва̏скрс) people greet each other with «Христос васкрсе!» - «Ваистину васкрсе!».

Customs:
• dyeing eggs (фарбати јаја, бојити јаја)
• red eggs must be on the table; one is kept until the next Easter as a charm (чува̀ркућа)
• playing «туцање јајима» (egg tapping, cracking eggs against each other)
• at night children put out a basket for the Easter bunny (ускршњи зец), who brings gifts
title: Easter among Serbs

note:
Serbia has a day of jokes on April 1 too: «Дан првоаприлске шале».

What people shout:
• after pulling a prank: «Априлилили!»
• at a good joke: «Ба̏ш је фо̏ра!»

A joke is a good way to start a conversation with Serbian friends.
title: April 1 in Serbia

related.sr: Е̏ци, пе́ци, пе̑ц, ти си ма̑лӣ зе̑ц
related.en: Eci, peci, pec, you are a little hare

related.sr: Е̑н де̑н до̏ре, дубо̀ко је мо̑ре
related.en: En den dore, the sea is deep
A duck swims across the Sava

note:
A counting-out rhyme is a «броја̀лица» in Serbian, from the word бро̑ј (number). Such rhymes are used in games like жму̏рке and «између две ватре» (dodgeball).

Classic openings:
• «Еци, пеци, пец, ти си мали зец»
• «Ен ден доре, дубоко је море»
• «Плива патка преко Саве»
• «Иде маца око тебе»
title: Serbian counting-out rhymes

note:
In Serbian homes it is customary to take off your shoes at the door: «Изу́ва̄ње (ко̏д нас)!»

Hosts offer guests slippers (па̀пуче), so shoes come off in other people's homes too. If the hosts themselves say «Не изувајте се», you can keep your shoes on.

The verb: ѝзути се (pf.), изу́вати се (impf.).
title: Taking off your shoes at someone's home

note:
Someone who sneezes is told «На̀здравље!» - «bless you» (literally «to your health»).

Small children are sometimes told «Пис, мацо!» - «shoo, kitty!» as a playful reaction.

Words: ки́јати, ки́нути, кија̀вица.
title: Sneezing and «Пис, мацо!»

note:
A fan clenches a fist, chops the air with it and chants «Ср̀бија, Ср̀бија!»

For encouragement:
• «Идемо!»
• «А̀јмо, а̀јде сви̏ у на́пад!»
• «На̏пре̄д Ср̀бија!»
• «Го̑л!»

Partizan fans are гробари, Red Star fans are делије. The word «цигани» is considered offensive.
title: Serbian fans' chants

related.en: I have the whole world under my heels

note:
You may notice that most popular songs sung by women are about «revenge on an ex»: look how happy I am without you. Songs sung by men are about complaints: «I loved you, and you left me».

An example is «Три чаше»: the heroine drinks to each of her loves and says «цео свет сам под штиклама».
title: Serbian songs: women take revenge, men complain

note:
Informal Serbian (especially among young people) has a slang, ша̏тровачкӣ го̏во̄р, in which the second part of a word is moved to the front.

Examples:
• здра̏во - воздра
• бра̏те - тебра
• за́кон - конза
• гла́ва - вугла
• пи̑во - вопи
• ва́жи - жи̏ва
• ћа̏ле - ле́ћа

A catchphrase: «Мунзе конза» - «Zemun is the law».
title: Šatrovački slang: words backwards

note:
In Serbian homes a guest is welcomed with слатко: a tray is brought out with preserves, teaspoons (кашичице) and two glasses of water.

How to enjoy it:
1. Take a spoonful of the preserve.
2. Put the used spoon into one of the glasses.
3. Wash it down with water from the other glass.

It is a sign of hospitality. Do not confuse it with сла̏ткӣ ку̀пус, braised cabbage with red pepper, a favorite dish.
title: «Слатко» for guests

note:
The word во̀ће is collective: fruit and berries.

Rakija is named after the fruit it is made from:
• шљи̏ва - plums
• ка̀јсија - apricots
• кру̏шка - pears

So if you are offered a «кајсија» in winter, it is not an apricot.

Berries are usually plural: купине, малине, рибизле.
title: Fruits, berries and the names of rakija

note:
What to take on a trip, in Serbian:
• прѐхлада - a cold
• диареја - diarrhea
• лек против температуре - fever reducer
• a remedy for bites (у̏јед)
• фластери, га́за, за́вој - adhesive bandages, gauze, bandage
• remedies for nausea and vomiting (мучнина, повраћање)
• a medicine for a sore throat (упала грла)
• креме са заштитним фактором и после сунчања - sunscreen and after-sun cream

A send-off wish: «Сре̏ћан пу̑т!»
title: A travel first-aid kit

related.en: «Браћу не доносе роде» («Storks don't bring brothers»), a children's song

note:
The children's song «Браћу не доносе роде» lists Serbian regions: Сре̑м and Ба̑нат. Both are in Војво̀дина, in the north.

The text also has:
• «купус из Срема» - mentioned as a joke
• ду̀ћа̄н - shop
• по̀родилиште - maternity hospital
title: Srem and Banat in songs

note:
Small boys, strangers' or one's own, are addressed as «бато!», girls as «се́ка», a son or a daughter as «си̑не!».

Кли̑нци means kids. The word бра̏т has a broad meaning in Serbian: it can be used for any male relative.

More words: новоро̀ђе̄нче, бе́ба, малѝшан.
title: How people address children

note:
The favorite place of Serbs is Greece: Halkidiki (Kassandra) and the islands of Thasos, Zakynthos, Skiathos and Кр̏ф (Corfu).

Other destinations:
• Montenegro is seen as close and not very interesting; Бу̑два is for young people
• in Turkey - Kuşadası and Marmaris
• at home - thermal spas (бање: Врњачка Бања, Сокобања, Про̀лом Ба̏ња) and mountains (Та̏ра, Златибор, Копаоник)

Duty free is called «фри шоп».
title: Where Serbs go on vacation

related.en: right into someone's ear (of musicians playing up close to one guest)

note:
Трубачи are folk brass bands whose playing sets the mood at weddings and in кафане (traditional taverns).

They do not play for free: when the band comes to your table, it is customary to give them money, sometimes even tucking it into the trumpet.

The song «Нѐсаница» is from the repertoire that is often played «на увце», right into a guest's ear.
title: Brass bands (трубачи)

note:
Like «Kleenex» or «Band-Aid» in English: a brand has become the common name.
• any toothpaste is каладонт (калодо̏нт)
• any chocolate spread is еурокрем (Nutella too)
• any adhesive bandage is хансапласт, although Serbian also has the word фла̏стер
title: Brand names used as common nouns

note:
Patterns on clothes:
• ша́ра, дѐзен - a pattern in general
• штрафте - stripes
• туфне, туфнице - polka dots
• ка̏ро (карирана кошуља) - checks
• цвѐтнӣ дѐзен - floral
• једнобојна одећа - plain clothes
• камуфлажни дезен, војнички дезен - camouflage, military print

Special names: «ћуркице» - paisley, «пепито» - houndstooth.
title: Patterns on clothes

related.sr: Јо̏ш је̏дна пе̏сма о ма̏лој га̏равој
related.en: «Још једна песма о малој гаравој» («Another Song About the Little Dark-Haired Girl»)

related.sr: ма̏ла га̏рава, цр̏на ка̏о бра̏ћа Ара̀пи
related.en: a little dark-haired girl, black as our Arab brothers

note:
In Đorđe Balašević's song «Још једна песма о малој гаравој» blondes are called:
• крво̀пије
• анаконде
• дражесни паразити
• барбике

The hero wants «малу гараву, црну као браћа Арапи» instead.

The song shows a playful, self-ironic attitude to types of women.
title: Blondes in a Balašević song

note:
Serbian also names teeth by numbers:
• «једѝнице и дво̏јке» - incisors (секутићи)
• «тро̏јке» - canines (очњаци)
• «чѐтворке и пѐтице» - premolars (преткутњаци)
• «шестице, седмице, осмице» - molars (кутњаци)

The eighth is the у̏мњак (wisdom tooth).

Baby teeth are мле̑чнӣ, permanent ones ста̑лнӣ.
title: Teeth by number

note:
По̀врће means vegetables.

Onions are told apart by color:
• цр̑нӣ лу̏к - the common onion (literally «black onion»)
• бе̑лӣ лу̏к - garlic (literally «white onion»)
• црвени лук - red onion
• млади лук - green onion
• пра̀зилук - leek

Peppers:
• па̀прика - the vegetable
• ба̀бура - bell pepper
• љута паприка - hot pepper
• бѝбер - black pepper

Also: ро̀тквица - radish, ре̏н - horseradish, ти̏квица - zucchini.
title: Vegetables in Serbian

note:
In Serbia September 1 is Дан знања: the start of the school year.

Someone who celebrates every holiday is said to «слави све живо»: celebrates anything and everything.
title: Knowledge Day

related.en: a good catch (said by a woman)

note:
Colloquial words for men:
• шме̏кер - a charming ladies' man
• фа̑ца - a rich, arrogant macho
• фра̏јер - a good catch (said by a woman)
• папу̀чар - a henpecked husband
• ма̀нгуп - a scamp
• ло́ла - a womanizer
• бѝта̄нга - a scoundrel
• бара̀ба - a troublemaker
• зве̏рка - a big shot

A neutral one is «госпо̀дин чо̏век»: a decent man.
title: Male types in Serbian

note:
Salon services:
• депила̀ција ног (целих или пола), рук, пре̏пона, пазуха, наусница, ле́ђа, гру̑ди - hair removal of the legs (full or half), arms, groin, armpits, upper lip, back, chest
• бразилска депилација - Brazilian waxing

Types of wax: хла̑днӣ (cold), топли (hot). Шећерна паста is sugaring.
title: Hair removal in Serbian

related.sr: ѝма̄м за̀казано ко̏д фризѐра у су̀боту
related.en: I have an appointment at the hairdresser's on Saturday

note:
A popular service in Serbia is фени̏ра̄ње: a wash and blow-dry, straightened or curled. It is inexpensive.

You book ahead: «имам заказано код фризера у суботу».

Ши̏ша̄ње is a haircut. «Траје сат времена» means it takes an hour.
title: At the hairdresser's

skip: About not building Serbian diminutives on the Russian model (-ушка, -ич); makes sense only for a Russian speaker

related.sr: Жѐлим ти да до̀бијеш све̏ што̏ не̑маш, а жѐлиш. И за̀држиш све̏ што̏ и̏маш, а во̏лӣш.
related.en: I wish you to get everything you don't have but want, and to keep everything you have and love.

related.sr: Жѐлим ти океа̀не здра̏вља, мо̏ра сре̏ће и љу́бави, је̏зера у̀спеха, рѐке па̏ра...
related.en: I wish you oceans of health, seas of happiness and love, lakes of success, rivers of money...

note:
Sample wishes (the translations are in the related words):
• «Желим ти да добијеш све што немаш, а желиш. И задржиш све што имаш, а волиш.»
• «Желим ти океане здравља, мора среће и љубави, језера успеха, реке пара...»

Children's birthdays are often held in a рођендаоница (a play room for parties). A song: «Ди̑ван да̑н».

Words: чѐститка, по́зӣвница, по̀клон, то̑рта.
title: Birthday wishes

note:
The vocabulary topic «Човек» (the human being): гла́ва, чѐло, ли́це, о̀браз, о̏брва, но̑с, у́ста, у̏сна, нѐпце, јѐзик, ја̏годице, гр̏ло, ждре́ло, у̏хо.

Gender quirks:
• о̏ко is neuter, but о̏чи (eyes) is feminine: лепе очи, њене очи
• уши is also feminine: његове уши
• у́ста is neuter and plural
title: Parts of the body: head and face

related.en: rolled pie of thin dough with meat or cheese

note:
The basis of the Serbian diet is bread, meat and yogurt.

In a bakery everything baked is пѐциво, either сла̑но (savory) or сла̀тко̄ (sweet):
• ђѐврек - a sesame bagel
• ки́фла - a roll for sandwiches
• погачица са чварцима - a bun with cracklings (чва̏рци)
• бу̀рек - a rolled pie of thin dough with meat or cheese
• мѐкика - a fried oblong doughnut
• ка̀јзерица - a dense roll
title: At the bakery: what пециво is

related.en: the company that made scratch-off lottery tickets

note:
Греб-греб (from грѐбати, to scratch) was the name of a company that made scratch-off lottery tickets. The name became generic: any such tickets are called that. The general word for them is сре̏ћка.

The slogan «Огреби срећу!» plays on the meaning of сре̏ћа: both happiness and luck.
title: «Греб-греб» and luck

related.en: to get tanned, literally «to turn black»
to get tanned, literally «to get color»

note:
In Serbia a tan is a sign that a person has had a good rest. It is customary to say to a tanned acquaintance:
• «Баш сте поцрнели»
• «Добила си боју»

Literally поцр̀нети means «to turn black», but it sounds like praise.
title: A tan as a compliment

note:
In Montenegro and in ijekavian dialects people say ђе̏ instead of где̏. The famous Montenegrin song «Ђе се купаш?» parodies the speech of young men on the beach.

It mixes ijekavian forms with standard ekavian ones:
• смје̏шта̄ј - сме̏шта̄ј
• ље̏то - ле̏то
• мјеста - ме̑ста̄
title: Ђе instead of где

related.en: to smell (give off a scent); to sniff
to rent (as a tenant); to rent out

note:
Serbian has words that mean two opposite things:
• мирѝсати - both to give off a smell and to smell something
• поза́јмити - both to borrow and to lend
• изна́јмити - both to rent and to rent out

The context shows which is meant, but even bilinguals mix up the direction of the action because of this.
title: One word, two opposite meanings

note:
На̀родњак is popular Serbian music in a folk spirit: it is sung at weddings and in the кафана.

Turbo-folk is a later style with modern arrangements and explicit lyrics.

Many hits were written to Greek melodies, and vice versa.
title: Narodnjak and turbo-folk

note:
Nurseries (ја̀слице) take children up to three, then comes the вр̀тић (also о̀бданиште, за̀бавӣште).

The last year before school is the прѐдшколско: school preparation, required by law.

Kindergartens get cute names: Ба̑јка, Бубама́ра, Ве̏верица, Ду́га, Зво̀нчић, Масла́чак, Су̑нце, Чаро̀лија.

A kindergarten teacher is a васпѝтач or васпита̀чица, a nanny is да̀диља.
title: Kindergartens in Serbia

skip: Russian calques in Serbian: literal translations from Russian; makes sense only for a Russian speaker

note:
Halloween is seen as a Catholic holiday, and in Serbia it is observed mostly where it pays: shops, bars, clubs. There is no craze.

Asked about «но̑ћ вѐштица», a Serb often replies with irony, as if to say, what Halloween?

But the Serbian words on the topic are worth knowing: баба Рога, вуко̀длак, ши̏шмиш, стра̏шило.
title: Halloween in Serbia

related.en: family feast of the patron saint

note:
Сла̏ва is the day of the family's patron saint. Each family keeps its own slava, and the date and customs pass from generation to generation. The feast is usually held in the home of the senior man of the family.

Always on the table:
• a candle
• славска погача
• red wine
• ко̏љӣво

An invitation is an honor: declining is not done, and once you have gone, it is polite to invite the hosts to your own slava in return.

Gifts: alcohol for the host, flowers or coffee for the hostess, chocolate for the children.
title: Slava, the family feast

note:
In Serbia a cat is called with «мац-мац», a dog with «кс-кс», and a dog barks «ав-ав».

Commands:
• «дођи!» - come here
• «седи!», «лези!» - sit, lie down
• «ста̏ни!» or «сто̑ј!» - stay
• «уз ногу!» - heel
• «пу̑стӣ!» - let go
• «остави то!» - leave it
• «ку̏ћи!» - go home

Praise: «до̏бар па̏с!», «бра̏во!»

To send a dog away: «бежи тамо!», or ruder, «мрш!»
title: Commands for a dog in Serbian

related.en: the second evening of New Year, January 1
family feast of the patron saint

note:
In Serbia New Year is a cheerful holiday but not the main one: Сла̏ва, Бо̀жић and У̏скрс matter more.

How it is celebrated:
1. The celebration (до̀чек) starts in the daytime, with дневне журке in bars: tables are booked in advance, and there is live music.
2. Toward evening many people go home to rest.
3. At midnight they go to the square for a concert and ва̏тромет (fireworks).

The evening of January 1 is the реприза Нове године, a second holiday.

Gifts are mostly for children.
title: New Year in Serbia

related.en: young oak branches burned on Christmas Eve
the first guest in the house

note:
January 6 is Бадњи дан, the last day of the fast. In the evening people burn the ба̏дња̄к: young oak branches.

January 7 is Бо̀жић, the main family holiday; shops are closed.

On the table at lunch:
• sprouted wheat
• a candle
• цѝцвара
• че̏сница with a coin

The first guest is the по̀ложајник.

The greeting: «Христос се роди!» - «Ваистину се роди!»
title: Christmas Eve and Christmas
